text:
Marathon Petroleum climbed 3.4% today, recovering sharply after a rough week that saw the stock down 8.6% since early November. The bounce came as oil prices stabilized—U.S. crude held steady near $100 a barrel—and refineries ramped up to 94.5% capacity utilization. After days of uncertainty tied to Iran tensions and peace talk whiplash, investors appear to have regained some confidence in the refining outlook, particularly with strong crude availability (nearly 692 million barrels in storage) supporting margins.

The stock's recovery also reflects a broader shift in market expectations. Early-week headlines raised hopes for a near-term Iran deal that could flood markets with cheap oil and crush refiner profits; more recent comments from Trump administration officials acknowledging diplomatic stalemate have tamped down those ultra-bearish scenarios. Refiners like Marathon benefit from a stable-to-firm crude environment, and today's move suggests that worst-case outcome may be priced out for now.
